item.research_question: How does a Permanent Parallel Magnetic Field (PPMF) of 9 T affect the electrodeposition current, mass deposition, and surface morphology of Ni-Co-Fe-Zn quaternary alloys compared to deposition without a magnetic field?
item.material_system: Ni-Co-Fe-Zn quaternary alloys deposited from a chloride solution containing 1 M NiCl2·6H2O, 0.25 M CoCl2·6H2O, 0.25 M FeCl2·4H2O, 0.25 M ZnCl2, and 0.5 M H3BO3
item.processing_route: Electrodeposition via chronoamperometry and cyclic voltammetry at -1.1, -1.2, and -1.3 V for 2400 seconds at 30-32°C and pH 4 ± 0.1, with and without a 9 T Permanent Parallel Magnetic Field (PPMF) applied parallel to the cathode surface
item.test_conditions: Temperature: 30-32°C; pH: 4 ± 0.1; Electrolyte: Chloride bath; Magnetic field: 9 T PPMF parallel to cathode; Duration: 2400 sec; Potentials: -1.1, -1.2, -1.3 V
key_findings: The percentage of current enhancement (Γ%) increased with more negative potentials: 11.9% at -1.1 V, 16.7% at -1.2 V, and 18.5% at -1.3 V for a 2400 sec duration.
Surface roughness (RMS) decreased from 48.5 nm to 23 nm at -1.1 V and from 112 nm to 39 nm at -1.3 V when the PPMF was applied.
The limiting current was enhanced in the presence of the PPMF, with current values increasing from 6.7 to 7.5 mA at -1.1 V, 18 to 20 mA at -1.2 V, and 27 to 32 mA at -1.3 V.
The mass of electrodeposition increased with the presence of the PPMF, with the difference in mass deposition ranging from 0.03 to 0.107 mg cm min-1.
The Content of Ni in the electrodeposited layers was always lower than the Composition Reference Line (CRL) due to anomalous behavior.
The lowest elemental content in the deposited layers belonged to Fe due to the chemical oxidation of Fe2+ to Fe3+ in the solution.
The morphology changed from polyhedral grains (without PPMF) to a nodular shape (with PPMF) at -1.10 V.
item.mechanism: The authors attribute the increased mass transport and current to the Magneto-Hydrodynamic (MHD) effect, largely caused by the Lorentz Force, which reduces the diffusion layer thickness. They also suggest that the magnetic field suppresses dendritic growth by reducing the effective potential at the tips of dendrites, leading to smoother surfaces.
item.limitations: The text notes that the solution was free of chelating reagents, which led to the lowest elemental content being Fe due to oxidation of Fe2+ to Fe3+, and states that the smoothness effect of an applied magnetic field on electrodeposition surfaces is still unclear.
quotes: The percentage of current enhancement (Γ%) was increased in the presence of PPMF, with results of Γ% = 11.9%, 16.7% and 18.5% at -1.1, -1.2 and -1.3 V respectively for a 2400 sec duration.
The MHD effect, (largely caused by the Lorentz Force) reduces the diffusion layer thickness, thus increasing the mass transport to the electrode surface.
At the applied voltage of -1.1 V, the roughness factor was reduced from 48.5 nm (7A; without PPMF) to 23 nm (7C; with PPMF).

Processing: Electrodeposition via chronoamperometry and cyclic voltammetry at -1.1, -1.2, and -1.3 V for 2400 seconds at 30-32°C and pH 4 ± 0.1, with and without a 9 T Permanent Parallel Magnetic Field (PPMF) applied parallel to the cathode surface.
